case_name: Yakub Abdul Razak Memon v State of Maharashtra, through Secretary, Home Department and others
respondent: State of Maharashtra, through Secretary, Home Department
facts: The conviction of the petitioner has been confirmed by this Court and the Review Petition as well as the Curative Petition filed by the petitioner have also been dismissed by this Court.
It is a fact that the sentence is to be executed on a certain date.
One more application made to His Excellency The Governor of Maharashtra is still pending.
The matter was partly heard yesterday and the arguments were deferred for today on this issue.
The synopsis portion of the Curative Petition reads as follows :-
The prayers in the Curative Petition read as follows:-(a) Allow the present curative petition filed against the order dated 9.4.2015 in Review Petition (Criminal) No. 474 of 2013;
Order XLVIII of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013 deals with Curative Petition and Rule 4(1) and (2) read as follows :-
'judgment' includes decree, order, sentence or determination of any Court, Tribunal, Judge or Judicial Officer.
The Judgment complained of (be it the order passed in the Review Petition) is passed by a Bench of three Judges comprising of Hon'ble Sh. Anil R. Dave, J., Hon'ble Sh. J. Chelameswar, J. and myself,
issues: What is the procedure for dealing with a Curative Petition?
Is there an error apparent on the face of the order in the Curative Petition?
Has the mandatory procedure prescribed under law been followed while dealing with the Curative Petition?
petitioner_arguments: One more application made to His Excellency The Governor of Maharashtra is still pending.
The submissions made about the Curative Petition do not appeal to me as they are irrelevant and there is no substance in them.
respondent_arguments: There is an error apparent on the face of the order in the Curative Petition.
The mandatory procedure prescribed under law has not been followed while dealing with the Curative Petition.
This is not an issue raised in the writ proceedings.
court_reasoning: In terms of the Judgment as defined under the Rules, a Curative Petition has to be circulated to a Bench of three senior-most Judges of this Hon'ble Court and the Judges who passed the Judgment complained of, if available.
The procedure prescribed under the law has been violated while dealing with the Curative Petition and that too, dealing with life of a person.
There is an error apparent on the face of the order in the Curative Petition.
The mandatory procedure prescribed under law has not been followed.

Though the learned senior counsel and the learned Attorney General referred to various grounds available in a Curative Petition, in the nature of the view I have taken in the matter that the Curative Petition itself has not been decided in accordance with the Rules prescribed by this Court, that defect needs to be cured first.
holding: The order dated 21.07.2015 passed in the Curative Petition is not as per the procedure prescribed under the Rules.
The Curative Petition has to be considered afresh in terms of the mandatory requirement under Rule 4 of Order XLVIII of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013.

The death warrant issued pursuant to the Judgment of the TADA Court dated 12.09.2006, as confirmed by this Court by its Judgment dated 21.03.2013, of which the Review Petition has been dismissed on 09.04.2015, is stayed till a decision afresh in accordance with law is taken in the Curative Petition.
cases_cited: Yakub Abdul Razak Memon v State of Maharashtra
